# Anna Farm Landscape Visualization

**Project:** Landscape Visualization, Proposal Support, and Review Delivery  
**Client:** Anna's Farm HOA  
**Contractor:** Sunrise Landscape Co.  
**Location:** Lafayette, Colorado

## Project Overview

This repository contains all materials for the Anna Farm landscape installation project, including:
- Design documentation and client needs specifications
- HTML proposal documents for client review
- Reference photography and annotated imagery
- AI-generated concept renders (daytime/nighttime)
- Prompts and technical pipeline artifacts

## Design Concept

A site-specific geological sculpture inspired by the Colorado landscape:
- **Flatirons-inspired groupings** of vertical Colorado red flagstone slabs
- **Canyon cliff walls** of Colorado red strip stone along creek bends
- **Dry creek bed** of river rock flowing through the composition
- **Boulder anchors** of native Colorado granite and river boulders

# Product Professor Agent Pack

**Product Professor** is a strict, AI-powered product and codebase review toolkit for Claude Code.

It does not just check whether your code compiles. It examines whether your product is actually good — whether it works, feels trustworthy, looks polished, handles real users, and is ready to ship. It grades the project like a demanding teacher: fair, specific, evidence-based, and not easily impressed.

> **True** (chanto shita) — roughly: "properly done, no shortcuts." The core question every audit answers.

---

## Requirements

- **Node.js 18+**
- **Claude Code** (claude.ai/code or VS Code extension)
- **git** (for safe-checks)
- **gh CLI** (optional — only needed for `publish-issues --apply`)

---

## Install

```bash
npm install -g product-professor
```

Then run inside the project you want to audit:

```bash
product-professor init
```

`init` copies skills and agents into your project's `.claude/` folder and asks 5 setup questions to create a product profile.

Check the install:
```bash
product-professor doctor
```

**No npm yet?** Clone and link locally:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/rikim811/product-professor-agent-pack ~/tools/product-professor
cd ~/tools/product-professor && npm install && npm link
cd /your/project && product-professor init
```

---

## Quick start (5 minutes)

```bash
# 1. Install the tool globally
npm install -g product-professor

# 2. Go to the project you want to audit and set it up
cd /your/project
product-professor init

# 3. Open Claude Code in your project and type in the chat:
/product-professor full

# 4. Claude runs the audit. Results land in:
#    docs/audits/YYYY-MM-DD-product-professor-review/

# 5. Generate a scorecard in Claude Code:
/score-product current

# 6. Record your baseline score (terminal):
product-professor record-score --auto "Baseline"
```

**The commands starting with `/` are typed in Claude Code's chat — not your terminal.**

---

## What the audit produces

```txt
docs/audits/YYYY-MM-DD-product-professor-review/
  AUDIT_REPORT.md        Full findings with executive verdict and letter grade
  SCORECARD.md           Weighted scores across 10 categories
  ISSUE_INDEX.md         All findings indexed by priority
  USER_COMPLAINTS.md     Realistic negative reviews from 5 user personas
  AI_GENERATED_FEEL.md   Why it looks AI-generated and how to fix it
  BUILD_HEALTH.md        Lint, typecheck, test, and build results
  DATABASE_SECURITY.md   Auth, permissions, and data ownership findings
  BEFORE_AFTER_SCORE.md  Score comparison after fixing (when run with 'after')
  PROMPTS.md             Exact follow-up prompts to run next
  issues/
    P0-001-missing-auth-check.md
    P1-001-empty-dashboard-state.md
    P2-001-no-pagination.md
```

**See a real example:** [`examples/example-scorecard.md`](./examples/example-scorecard.md)

---

Next.js frontend for the Tribes application. Communicates with a separate

- **Jest 30** + **@testing-library/react** — unit and component tests

- Node.js 20.15.0 (see `.nvmrc`)
- npm

## Local development

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Copy env and fill in values
cp .env.example .env.local

# Start dev server (Turbopack, port 8080)
npm run dev
```

App will be available at `http://localhost:8080`.

### Environment variables

| Variable             | Description                                   |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `API_URL`            | Laravel backend URL (server-side)             |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Telegram bot token for pre-push notifications |
| `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`   | Telegram chat ID for pre-push notifications   |

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev        # Dev server with Turbopack (port 8080)
npm run build      # Production build (Webpack)
npm run start      # Run production build
npm run lint       # ESLint check
npm run lint:fix   # ESLint autofix
npm run format     # Prettier format
npm test           # Jest unit tests
npm test -- --watch          # Watch mode
npm test -- --coverage       # With coverage report
npm run push       # Pre-push checks + git push
```

Feature Sliced Design (FSD):

```

  lib/        # Utilities, config, routes

readme: # airlayer An in-process semantic engine that compiles `.view.yml` definitions into dialect-specific SQL — and optionally executes queries against real databases. Built in Rust as both a library and CLI tool. ## Quick start ```bash bash <(curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oxy-hq/airlayer/main/install_airlayer.sh) ``` Then initialize a project within an empty directory: ```bash mkdir my-project && cd my-project airlayer init ``` This connects to your database, discovers your schema, and generates `config.yml`, `.view.yml` files, and [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) sub-agents for querying and building your semantic layer. ## Example Given an `orders.view.yml`: ```yaml name: orders table: public.orders dialect: postgres dimensions: - name: status type: string expr: status measures: - name: total_revenue type: sum expr: amount ``` You can query it with the CLI as follows: ```bash # add -x to execute against the database airlayer query \ --dimension orders.status \ --measure orders.total_revenue \ --filter orders.status:equals:active \ --limit 10 ``` Which will compile to the following SQL, returned to stdout: ```sql SELECT "orders".status AS "orders__status", SUM("orders".amount) AS "orders__total_revenue" FROM public.orders AS "orders" WHERE ("orders".status = 'active') GROUP BY 1 LIMIT 10 ``` ## Supported databases | Database | Dialect flag | Execution | |----------|-------------|-----------| | PostgreSQL | `postgres` | Native (TCP) | | MySQL | `mysql` | Native (TCP) | | BigQuery | `bigquery` | REST API (OAuth2) | | Snowflake | `snowflake` | REST API (session auth) | | DuckDB | `duckdb` | In-process (libduckdb) | | ClickHouse | `clickhouse` | HTTP API | | Databricks | `databricks` | SQL Statement API | | Redshift | `redshift` | Native (TCP, via Postgres wire protocol) | | Presto / Trino | `presto` | REST API (polling) | | SQLite | `sqlite` | In-process (libsqlite3) | | MotherDuck | `duckdb` | In-process (md: protocol) | | Domo | `domo` | REST API | All dialects support SQL compilation. # Company Inception Pipeline

A Claude Code workflow that accelerates moving from a high-level company idea to cold outreach for customer and expert validation meetings. Built for deep-tech and SaaS founders who want to systematically validate key assumptions before committing resources.

## What It Produces

Run through 5 stages and walk away with:

1. **Lean business model canvas** and business plan with prioritized assumptions
2. **Landscape map** showing how value flows between your company and major players across verticals
3. **Enriched company database** (100+ companies with domains and descriptions)
4. **Contact list** with verified email addresses for decision-makers at target companies
5. **Cold outreach campaigns** — 3-email sequences ready to load into Hunter.io Campaigns for sending

## Prerequisites

- A [Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/claude) subscription (required — powers the entire pipeline)
- [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) CLI installed
- A [Hunter.io](https://hunter.io) paid plan (required — free tier is too limited for meaningful company and contact discovery)
- A [Tavily](https://tavily.com) API key (free tier may suffice for small runs)
- Hunter.io Campaigns (included with your Hunter.io plan) handles the cold outreach sending — the pipeline outputs map directly to its sequencer fields

## Setup

1. **Clone the repository:**

   ```bash
   git clone <repo-url>
   cd company-inception-pipeline
   ```

2. **Create your local settings file** by copying the template and removing the `example.` prefix:

   ```bash
   cp .claude/example.settings.local.json .claude/settings.local.json
   ```

   The file must be named `settings.local.json` for Claude Code to pick it up.

3. **Add your API keys** — open `.claude/settings.local.json` and replace the placeholder values:

   ```json
   {
     "env": {
       "TAVILY_API_KEY": "your-actual-tavily-key",
       "HUNTER_API_KEY": "your-actual-hunter-key"
     }
   }
   ```

   This file is gitignored — your keys won't be committed.

   > **Important:** Only put your API keys in `.claude/settings.local.json`. Do NOT edit `.mcp.json` — that file uses `${VARIABLE_NAME}` references that are resolved automatically from your local settings. If you paste keys directly into `.mcp.json`, they will be committed to git.

4. **Personalize CLAUDE.md** — open `CLAUDE.md` and replace the following to make it yours:
   - Replace `"Brett"` with your name (search for all occurrences)
   - Replace `"The vibes are bad, dawg"` with whatever phrase you'd prefer Claude to use when it has a gut feeling something is off but can't articulate why

5. **Start Claude Code** from the project directory:

   ```bash
   claude
   ```

## Running the Pipeline

Each stage is a slash command. Run them in order — each stage reads the previous stage's outputs.

```text
/brainstorm-company
```

# Agent Flow Simulator

Um app que ensina a arquitetura de contexto (AGENTS.md, SKILLS, MCP,
SUBAGENTS) **mostrando visualmente** o caminho que um agente percorre pra
decidir o que consultar, dado um pedido do usuário.

Você digita (ou escolhe) um pedido, tipo "cria um componente de botão",
e vê o diagrama acender, em sequência, os nós que um agente real
consultaria pra atender aquele pedido — com a explicação do porquê em
cada passo.

Além dos cenários de exemplo, o app tem dois modos de análise **real**:

- **GitHub público** — aponta pra qualquer repo público e o server
  busca o AGENTS.md, skills e subagents de verdade via API REST do GitHub
- **Pasta local (MCP)** — aponta pra uma pasta na máquina e o server lê
  os arquivos via um cliente MCP de verdade, conectando no servidor
  oficial `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`

Repare que cada modo usa a ferramenta certa pro problema — API direta
pro GitHub (não é um agente falando com outro agente), MCP de verdade

## 1. OVERVIEW

### What This Framework Does

AI coding assistants have amnesia. Every session starts from zero. You explain your architecture Monday. By Wednesday, it is gone. Decisions, trade-offs, the carefully reasoned choices behind them, all lost the moment the conversation window closes. This framework fixes that.

The framework adds three layers on top of the base platform:

1. **Structured documentation** (Spec Kit) - every file change gets a spec folder recording what changed, why and how. Like a lab notebook for software.
2. **Packet continuity** (files) - session context written into the spec folder it belongs to, then found again through a committed trigger index and ripgrep recipes over the same files.
3. **Coordinated agents and skills** - 12 specialized agents routed by a gate system that loads the right skills at the right time.

# AI Validation Framework

A working implementation of the **PRESS** progressive validation framework: five
principles carried through a ten-week journey, with templates to run it and a
dependency-free CLI to score it.

```
Design            Dogfood           Alpha             Beta
weeks 1-2         weeks 3-4         weeks 5-6         weeks 7-10
What should       Does it work      Do friendly       Can it scale
we build?         for us?           users like it?    safely?
```

Validation works like building a house: a foundation, then a structure, then
floors. Skip a step and everything above it collapses. Each phase answers one
question, embeds all five PRESS principles from day 1, and ends at a gate you
can actually check rather than a date you can quietly slip.

## The five principles

| | Principle | The question it forces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **P** | People-first | Does this make the people using it more capable? |
| **R** | Responsible | Does it treat every affected group fairly, and can we prove it? |
| **E** | Explainable | Can the people affected understand and repeat the reasoning? |
| **S** | Safe | What happens on the worst day, and can a human take back control? |
| **S** | Sustainable | Can we still afford to run this in two years? |

## Quickstart

Python 3.10+, no dependencies.

```bash
cd tools

# Start a project
python -m press init "Call Center Assistant" --start-date 2026-09-07

# Week 1: set a target and the metric that proves it, per principle
python -m press target explainable 7 \
  --metric "Share of decisions tracing to a nameable factor"

# Answer the validation criteria as evidence arrives
python -m press check E-1 pass --evidence "Agents explained 9/10 decisions unaided"

# Where are we, and what is blocking the next phase?
python -m press status
python -m press score
python -m press gate design

# Full markdown snapshot
python -m press report --out reports/week-2.md
```

`press score` and `press gate` exit non-zero when something is below target or
blocking, so both work as CI checks on the project file.

### Commands

| --- | --- |

| `measure <principle> <0-10> --evidence` | Record what you actually measured |

# peony

A fast, **incremental** ELF linker for x86-64 Linux, written in Rust. Drop-in
compatible with the `ld`/`cc` command line, so it can be the final linker for
`rustc`- and `gcc`-based toolchains.

**My thesis.** You edit one file and rebuild a thousand times a day but every
linker relinks the whole program from scratch, every time (mold and lld are
fast, but they still redo all of it). peony doesn't. A one-file change relinks in
**~19 ms** one-shot, or **~3–4 ms** with a resident daemon, versus a ~32 ms full
link and the result is **byte-for-byte identical to a full link**, every time.

## How

A relink does work proportional to what *changed*, not to the size of the program:

| change | what peony does | one-`.o` relink (402-object program) |
|---|---|---|
| nothing | reuse the output untouched (stat cache) | instant |
| one file | re-parse only that `.o`, reuse the cached layout + symbol table, patch its bytes in place | **~19 ms** |
| + daemon | keep the layout + symbols resident in RAM | **~3–4 ms** |

The fast path is taken only when peony's cache gates establish the output should
be identical: same sizes, same symbols, same GOT/PLT/TLS demand, no
`--gc-sections`/`--icf`, no archive change. Anything else falls back to a full
link. **peony never serves stale bytes**; that is the one rule everything else
bends to.

Incremental is on by default. For the daemon, `export PEONY_DAEMON=1` and peony
spawns and reuses one automatically.

## Correctness Story

The real correctness gate is differential testing against the system linker:
peony links real objects and checks byte identity against a full link across the
incremental, daemon, and thread-count paths.

`rocq-tests/` holds machine-checked Rocq/Coq model proofs. They are useful
specifications for linker invariants, but they are not whole-program
verification of the Rust implementation. Public verification wording is scoped
by [`docs/VERIFICATION_CLAIMS.md`](docs/VERIFICATION_CLAIMS.md), with the
machine-readable source in
[`docs/VERIFICATION_CLAIMS.json`](docs/VERIFICATION_CLAIMS.json). That table
separates model-only results, bridge-tested correspondences, theorem bridges,
and narrow implementation-verified surfaces.

- Rocq theorem bridges and assumption audits:
  [`docs/THEOREM_TO_RUST_BRIDGES.md`](docs/THEOREM_TO_RUST_BRIDGES.md) maps
  theorem families to Rust surfaces, tests, trusted boundaries, and claim
  scopes. `docs/verification-assumptions/` stores the `Print Assumptions`
  outputs for theorem-backed public claims.
- Rust bridge and differential tests:
  `peony-cache/tests/partial_relink.rs`,
  `peony-emit::input_work` unit tests,
  `peony-reloc` byte-formula tests,
  `peony-layout/tests/layout_gc_bridge.rs`,
  `peony-layout/tests/icf_bridge.rs`, and
  `peony-symbols/tests/symbol_bridge.rs` exercise the matching concrete planner,

**Live demo:** [https://expense-tracker-production-370e.up.railway.app](https://expense-tracker-production-370e.up.railway.app)
> Demo credentials: `demo@spendly.com` / `demo123`

---

## Features

- **User accounts** — register, log in, and log out securely with hashed passwords
- **Expense management** — add, edit, and delete expenses with a clean form interface
- **7 categories** — Food, Transport, Bills, Health, Entertainment, Shopping, Other
- **Dashboard** — total spent, transaction count, and top spending category at a glance
- **Transaction history** — paginated list of recent expenses with date, category, and amount
- **Category breakdown** — visual bar chart showing spending distribution by category
- **Date filtering** — filter your dashboard by custom date ranges or quick presets (This month, 3 months, 6 months)
- **Toast notifications** — success feedback after adding, editing, or deleting expenses
- **CSRF protection** — all POST forms are protected with per-session CSRF tokens
- **Ownership enforcement** — users can only view, edit, and delete their own expenses

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend | Python 3.10+, Flask 3.1 |
| Database | SQLite (via Python's `sqlite3`) |
| Auth | Werkzeug password hashing |
| Frontend | Jinja2 templates, Vanilla JS, CSS custom properties |
| Server | Gunicorn (production) |
| Testing | pytest, pytest-flask |

No ORMs. No npm. No frontend frameworks. Just Flask, SQLite, and vanilla JS.

# SDD Pilot

Enhance your AI coding tool with a structured, spec-driven delivery workflow.

## What is SDD Pilot?

Most AI coding tools jump straight to code. SDD Pilot adds a [spec-driven development](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/ai-augmented-spec-driven-development-lifecycle-attila-szász-64e9f/) layer on top — so you specify *what* to build before *how* to build it.

- **Phase-by-phase process** — each feature moves through Specify → Plan → Tasks → Implement → QC
- **Quality gates** — you cannot skip ahead; each phase requires the previous phase's artifacts
- **Structured artifacts** — specs, plans, tasks, and QC reports live under `specs/<feature-folder>/`
- **Specialized agents** — a dedicated role (Product Manager, Architect, Engineer, QC) handles each phase
- **Autopilot mode** — run the full pipeline unattended with a single command

> **Runtime output:** Workflow and sub-agent communication is compact by default. Milestone updates prefer `done / issues / next`, while safety warnings, destructive actions, and parser-sensitive artifacts stay explicit.

> **Compatibility:** Works with **GitHub Copilot**, **Antigravity**, **Windsurf**, **OpenCode**, **Claude Code**, and **OpenAI Codex**.

> **Codex behavior:** Codex wrappers explicitly stop for user answers at interactive decision points instead of inferring the recommended option. `/sddp-autopilot` remains the explicit unattended exception.

> **Heritage:** SDD Pilot evolved from [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) ([0.0.90](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/releases/tag/v0.0.90)).

---

## How It Works

SDD Pilot has two workflows: an optional **project bootstrap** to set up shared context, and the **feature delivery** lifecycle you repeat for each feature.

# AI.econ

**Stranica uživo:** <https://MislavSag.github.io/CroAIcon>

AI.econ je Quarto analitički blog za hrvatske gospodarske podatke, GFI izvještaje i Eurostat serije. Projekt je pripremljen za rad u Positronu, uz R kao glavni analitički jezik i Python za izgradnju podataka i grafova.

**Kako sve radi:** za cjelovitu sliku (stil, grafovi, cijeli tijek od teme do objave i kako oba AI alata dijele isti mozak) pogledaj [`_workflow/how-it-works.md`](_workflow/how-it-works.md).

## Brzi start

```powershell
cd CroAIcon
Rscript scripts/update_data.R
quarto preview
```

Quarto preview koristi port `4200`, ako je slobodan.

## R paketi

Projekt radi bez automatskog `renv` aktiviranja. Za instalaciju paketa u standardnu R biblioteku:

```powershell
Rscript scripts/setup_r_packages.R
```

Ako želiš koristiti projektni `renv`, pokreni:

```powershell
$env:CROAICON_USE_RENV = "true"
Rscript scripts/setup_r_packages.R
```

`arrow` i `duckdb` mogu trajati dulje pri prvoj instalaciji, osobito na Windowsima.

## Otvaranje u Positronu

Otvori folder repozitorija ili datoteku `CroAIcon.Rproj`.

## Struktura

```text
posts/      Quarto blog postovi
R/          R funkcije za podatke, grafove, tablice i warehouse
python/     AI nacrti i pomoćne provjere
data/       Lokalni sirovi i obrađeni podaci, ignorirano u Gitu
outputs/    Generirane činjenice, tablice i grafovi
prompts/    Upute za AI generiranje nacrta
scripts/    Operativne skripte
```

## Data workflow

1. Sirovi GFI podaci idu u `data/raw/gfi/` ili u folder naveden kroz `GFI_SOURCE_DIR`.
2. Eurostat i GFI skripte pripremaju podatke u `data/processed/`.
3. Analitičke tablice mogu se spremiti u `data/warehouse/croaicon.duckdb`.
4. Provjerene brojke za AI nacrt idu u `outputs/facts/*.json`.
5. AI nacrt ide u `drafts/ai/`, a nakon provjere se ručno prebacuje u `posts/`.

## AI nacrt

Objavljeni postovi nastaju ručno. Build skripta (`python/*_build.py`) sprema tablice u `outputs/`, chart skripta (`python/*_charts.py`) crta PNG grafove, a tekst se piše u `posts/<slug>/index.qmd` s brojkama vezanim na `outputs/`. Cijeli tijek je u [`_workflow/how-it-works.md`](_workflow/how-it-works.md).

`ai_draft.py` je opcionalni pomoćnik koji od provjerenog facts JSON-a radi nacrt, sa ili bez OpenAI ključa. Nije dio žive objave.

Bez API poziva:

```powershell
python python/ai_draft.py --facts outputs/facts/example_facts.json --offline
```

S OpenAI API-jem:

1. Kopiraj `env.example` u `.env`.
2. Postavi `OPENAI_API_KEY` i `OPENAI_MODEL`.
3. Pokreni:

```powershell
python python/ai_draft.py --facts outputs/facts/example_facts.json
```

Skripta koristi OpenAI Responses API kada su dostupni ključ, model i paket `openai`. Ako nešto nedostaje, napravi offline strukturirani nacrt.

## Novi post

```powershell
Rscript scripts/new_post.R "Naslov nove analize"
```

## Komentari

Komentari su pripremljeni kroz Giscus u `_quarto.yml`.

```yaml

```

| `CLAUDE.md` | The playbook — phases, the agent/skill model, prefix registry |
| `.claude/agents/` | The 19 always-on agent definitions (14 domain + 5 core) |
| `skills/` | The skill library (`<name>/SKILL.md`) — domain + cross-cutting |
| `catalog.json` | Index of agents and skills (`name, pack, kind, scope, model, description`) for JIT selection |

| `Sync-AgentPacks.{ps1,sh}` | Stage a pack's domain skills into a project (invoked by `ccds sync`) |
| `Verify-Agents.ps1` / `verify-agents.sh` | Validate agents and skills against ADR-0001 invariants |
| `build-release.ps1` | Build reproducible release ZIP + sidecar SHA256 |
| `scripts/jit-claude.md` | Canonical source for the ccds pointer block injected into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Tag-driven release build + GitHub Release publication |
| `DECISIONS.md` | Architecture decision records (ADR-0001 … ADR-0009) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Session-by-session history |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Contribution terms |
| `LICENSE` | PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 |

### Installed layout

```
~/.claude/
  agents/          ← 19 always-on agents (14 domain + 5 core; always loaded)
  skills/          ← cross-cutting skills (always available)
  playbook/        ← managed by installer
    bin/           ← ccds dispatcher (ccds.ps1 / ccds.sh / ccds symlink)

Collection of compute graph analysis tools for realistic performance modeling across many different hardware platforms.

```bash

Cybersecurity awareness training platform disguised as a post-apocalyptic data center management game. Built by [Matrices GmbH](https://matrices.de).

**Tech stack:** SvelteKit 2 (Svelte 5) + Fastify 5 + PostgreSQL + Redis + Drizzle ORM

```bash
git clone git@github.com:TheMorpheus407/the-dmz.git
cd the-dmz
pnpm install

pnpm db:migrate              # run database migrations
pnpm db:seed                 # seed development data

`pnpm dev` runs a preflight check that verifies Docker services are running and required ports are available. If something is wrong, you'll get a clear error message.

- `Debug Vitest (current file)`: runs the currently open test file with Vitest debug flags.
- `Debug Playwright (current file, headed)`: runs the currently open E2E test in headed debug mode.
